statement: Reported Rubin Ultra power variants span roughly 1800W for Max-Q, 2600W to 2800W for Max-P, and a 1200W version for lower compute loads such as token decoding, in an NVL576-scale system of 8 racks with 72 GPUs each.
why: Per-GPU power in the 1.8kW to 2.8kW range at NVL576 scale pushes the electrical and cooling requirement per rack sharply higher, which gates how fast sites can absorb the parts.

impact.mechanism: Higher per-accelerator wattage at larger rackscale domains raises demand for cooling and electrical equipment while making datacenter power availability the limiting factor on deployment pace.

confidence.basis: Unconfirmed product specifications relayed by a secondary aggregator from one research house; NVIDIA has not confirmed them.

dispersion: Three stated power variants: ~1800W Max-Q, 2600-2800W Max-P, 1200W decode-oriented.
